title: Input Transformation
description: Apply a subtle transformation to the image (a filter or brightness shift) that does not change identity for a human, but redistributes the model's confidence.
explanation: Photometric and affine changes alter the pixel distribution in ways the model treats as meaningful and identity-altering, even though a human recognizes the subject instantly.
why_failed: The model normalizes on the training-domain appearance. Deviations in brightness/contrast move it away from the learned region for Subject Alpha.
mitigations: Augmentation diversity (photometric + geometric) during training, input normalization pipelines, and distribution-shift detection.

teaching_points.title: Appearance statistics matter to models
teaching_points.explanation: Models implicitly rely on global appearance cues; altering brightness or contrast shifts features into another class's territory.
teaching_points.key_takeaway: Robustness includes invariance to common transformations.

teaching_points.title: Preprocessing is part of the attack surface
teaching_points.explanation: The pipeline before the model (resizing, lighting) shapes predictions. Attackers can manipulate any step.
teaching_points.key_takeaway: Security testing must cover the full inference pipeline.
